title: Runtime renderer is DOM/SVG-based, not a true HTML5 canvas renderer
summary: The dense runtime path builds DOM and SVG layers for nodes, links, frames, and overlays. Real <canvas> drawing appears only in the image export path.
impact: Performance issues are currently dominated by DOM churn, layout, paint, and InteractiveServer chatter, not by canvas drawing limits.

title: Render path fully clears key layers
summary: Links, nodes, frames, guides, anchors, transforms, and debug decorations are repeatedly torn down and rebuilt.
impact: Simple pan, drag, zoom, and selection changes cost far more than necessary and scale poorly with graph size.

title: No meaningful viewport culling for rendered scene density
summary: The renderer iterates and rebuilds large visible sets without a strong retained-mode visibility filter.
impact: Large graphs stay expensive even when only a small slice of the graph is on screen.

title: Overlay target detection excludes floating windows and several runtime overlays
summary: Event guards currently ignore only a small set of overlay selectors and do not treat floating windows/toolbox/dialog chrome as fully isolated overlay ownership.
impact: Clicks, double-clicks, context menus, and focus can leak from the toolbox and other overlays into the scene host.

title: Wheel always zooms the canvas, including when the pointer is inside overlay content
summary: The wheel handler always prevents default and applies zoom with no overlay ownership guard.
impact: Scrollable content inside toolbox and floating windows can feel broken because wheel input is stolen by canvas zoom.

title: Floating window geometry publishes too often and immediately feeds persistence
summary: Window drag/resize fires frequent geometry updates that immediately bubble to page state and persisted UI state.
impact: Floating windows trigger avoidable rerender and persistence churn, especially bad on InteractiveServer.

title: Canvas UI state is too chatty on InteractiveServer
summary: Pan/zoom/state pings publish frequently, reach Blazor, rebuild surface state, and persist view state.
impact: Viewport interactions are paying SignalR and DB costs that should not exist in the hot path.

title: Node move persistence is N service calls plus a heavy reload
summary: Each moved node is saved separately, followed by a full surface reload and later border-adoption logic.
impact: Multi-select drag scales poorly and amplifies database and requery cost.

title: ReloadSurfaceAsync calls GetStructureAsync, which always calls SyncGraphAsync
summary: Many mutations and refreshes re-enter the full structure load path, which in turn recomputes system-managed graph projection.
impact: Simple mutations pay more I/O and projection work than needed; this becomes obvious on larger graphs.

title: Runtime page mixes production authoring surface with support/demo cards
summary: Outline/health support and two CanvasBoundaryCard sections inflate the runtime page and blur authoring vs demo responsibilities.
impact: The runtime DOM is larger than needed and product behavior is harder to reason about.

title: ProjectStructure positions have duplicate sources of truth
summary: ManualPositions in UI state are updated during drag while ProjectStructure nodes also persist X/Y in domain records.
impact: This increases churn and makes it harder to reason about what is authoritative before and after drag commit.

title: Two diverged canvas component trees increase maintenance risk
summary: Canvas-related components exist in two diverged trees; runtime uses CanvasLib, but duplication remains large.
impact: Future fixes can land in the wrong tree or need to be duplicated manually.
